text:
laura: RFC follow-up: proposing an incremental 'suture' adapter for model-routing/session-proxy. Instead of ripping the surface out, we let a tiny adapter handle normalization and route ownership per-tenant. Main goals: minimize blast radius, enable fast rollback, and allow A/B parity checks.

henry: quick question  what's the hot-path overhead?

laura: estimate 0.5-3ms depending on branch (fast path vs auth check). small but measurable. we'll perf it in the spike.

maya: parity how do we detect semantic regressions? hashes +- not great for some prompts.

laura: two-stage detection: (1) lightweight response-hash sampling, (2) targeted semantic evals for any flagged requests. also nightly deterministic regression run against core prompt set.

henry: cache mismatch is a risk. If new svc uses different KV layout we need normalization + backward-compat.

laura: adapter will provide key normalization and a compatibility shim. feature-flag toggles legacy vs strict normalization.

simon: rollout guard: per-tenant rate limiter + slow linear ramp. prefer doubling is aggressive for big tenants. propose per-tenant token-bucket start 0.5% then *1.5 every 30m until 100% or failure.

laura: good point. I'll change ramp to 0.5% start, multiplier 1.5, interval 30m. sample snippet: 
```
rollout:
  name: "suture-adapter"
  per_tenant_ramp: { start_fraction: 0.005, multiplier: 1.5, interval_mins: 30, max_fraction: 1.0 }
  monitors: ["response-hash-rate", "latency-p95", "errors"]
  auto_actions: { "diff_rate>0.3%": "pause_ramp", "error_rate>0.8%": "rollback" }
```

maya: include semantic score checks in monitors (intent-stability, slot-extraction match). hash diffs for signal, semantic checks for actioning.

laura: yup. flagged prompts go to eval pipeline with semantic checks.

henry: where do flags live? we need an authoritative per-tenant flag store.

laura: config-service will hold flags, runtime reads via feature-proxy with 5s TTL. infra will add invalidate hook for deploys.

infra-bot: Created INF-460: "feature-proxy: per-tenant routing flags + invalidation hooks". Owner: infra-team. ETA: 72h. https://tracker/redwood/INF-460

simon: observability asks: dashboard tiles for percent routed to suture, per-tenant ramp curve, diff-rate heatmap, and visible migration ids.

laura: will add dash spec to RFC addendum. also adding X-Migration-Id header to all suture requests for cross-service querying.

maya: lifecycle question: when should we remove adapters? they shouldn't be permanent.

laura: lifecycle policy proposal: after 14 days with <0.1% semantic diffs and >95% of traffic on new service, mark for auto-prune. ops reviews batch and schedules pruning window.

henry: tests: integration harness that simulates KV skew, induced latency, error storms, and verifies rollback triggers. include load tests with varied prompt lengths.

laura: adding an automated test matrix in spike. will include perf targets and rollback playbook.

simon: small ops nit: include a migration-name + owner in headers and traces so we can filter logs quickly.

laura: added: X-Migration-Id and X-Migration-Owner header; wire into tracing tags.

henry: once addendum posted I'll review perf section.

laura: posting addendum EOD with rollout plan, dash mockups, test matrix, and cutover checklist. thanks for the quick input.
